description: Ring-RPT CSG pebble k=1.39333 vs OpenMC 1.36479 (+2854 pcm). Miss is concentrated in resonance escape p (+9%, 0.528 vs 0.484) and fast fission eps (-6%, 1.411 vs 1.504); eta/f match <1%. SiC S(a,b) ruled out (+105 pcm, 1sigma). Leading hypothesis: U-238 URR (~20-150 keV) self-shielding not reconstructed by Nuclide::from_endf_file - OpenMC's NNDC ACE carries PURR probability tables, the on-device RECONR+BROADR path does not wire UNRESR/PURR (see op-cjw.6). ACTION: dump reconstructed U-238 sigma_gamma(E) from from_endf_file at 6.7eV/20.9eV resolved resonances (expect match) and 20/50/100 keV URR band (expect ours low + structureless), compare to the endfb-viii.0-hdf5 library OpenMC used. If confirmed, real fix is wiring PURR into the reconstruction path (njoy-outram-park-fork, coordinate op-cjw.6).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
CORRECTION 2026-09-10 (measured, see op-sdbk): the leading hypothesis in this bead is wrong, and its predicted sign is backwards.

1. U-238 in ENDF/B-VIII.0 carries LSSF=1 in its LRU=2 range (MF=2/MT=151, the CONT after the energy-dependent-AP TAB1). LSSF=1 means the URR parameters are for SELF-SHIELDING ONLY and MF=3 already holds the infinitely-dilute unresolved cross sections. MF=3/MT=102 is 0.0 b below 20 keV, jumps to 0.52987 b, and runs down to 0.14114 b at 150 keV.

2. Our reconstruction REPRODUCES those values to within 0.08% from 24 keV to 150 keV (examples/u238_urr_probe.rs, --features endf-pebble-cases). So 'expect ours low + structureless' is half wrong: structureless yes, low no. The ACTION as written would have measured this and stopped.

3. Sign check: self-shielding REDUCES effective capture, so probability tables RAISE k. OpenMC (with PURR tables) is the LOWER of the two (1.36479 vs our 1.39333). Wiring PURR into the reconstruction path would therefore move this case FURTHER from OpenMC, not closer. The +2854 pcm cannot be missing URR self-shielding.

4. What IS real: op-sdbk -- BROADR has no thnmax bound, so SIGMA1 runs across the resolved/unresolved boundary and collapses the 20 keV seam from 0.530 b to 0.291 b, an error interpolated over 20-24 keV. Right sign to inflate k, but 0.18 lethargy units wide -- tens to low hundreds of pcm, not 2854.

So the bulk of the +2854 pcm is still unexplained and this bead stays open. Note the miss is ALSO -6% in fast fission eps (1.411 vs 1.504), which is MeV-range physics that no URR treatment touches -- worth re-reading as its own lead rather than as a knock-on of p.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 hypothesis refuted by code read, no run needed (recording so nobody re-raises it): the epsilon miss (-6%) is NOT a fission-spectrum stand-in. keff_delta.rs:835 banks in-transport fission neutrons via nuc.sample_fission_energy -> sample_chi (nuclide.rs:886), which dispatches the full ENDF MF=5 law set: ContinuousTabular, Watt, Tabulated, Maxwell LF=7, Evaporation LF=9, WattEnergyDependent LF=11, and Mixture with TAB1-weighted law selection. So fission neutrons are born from each nuclide's REAL chi at the actual incident energy. The fixed Watt at keff_delta.rs:554/680 is the INITIAL source only and is washed out by the 30 inactive generations.

Note this also means the caveat carried in examples/htr10_fuel_zone_kinf.rs ('a flat nu-bar and a Watt fission-spectrum stand-in', citing nuclide.rs:196-199/:1110-1124, 'worth about +500 pcm on Godiva') describes the LOW/CORE tier and does NOT apply to the HIGH/ENDF path this ring-RPT case runs on. That caveat should be scoped per-tier where it appears, or it will keep being read as applying to results it does not.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 HYPOTHESIS linking the shared bias to the baseline drift, with its prediction stated before the fingerprint is run.

Established today (op-mzvp.2.8): on OpenMC's own reflective sphere, BOTH pebbles sit about +1700..1900 pcm above OpenMC (explicit +1681, ring-RPT +1875, differing by 194 pcm, inside noise). So the residual is one bias in the nuclear data, shared by both geometries — the RPT geometry and its fitted radius are ruled out.

Separately: the explicit-cube case moved -1632 pcm between 23cd2549 and 0cd9a22c, and U-238 reconstruction wall time fell 91.7 s -> 26.8 s over the same 33 njoy commits (waves 5/6/7: BROADR thnmax bound, the sigfig discontinuity shading, RECONR changes).

PUT TOGETHER: if the sphere shifted by roughly the same -1632 pcm the cube did, then at 23cd2549 the explicit-sphere case would have sat near 1.398, i.e. about +3300 pcm above OpenMC — which is the same ballpark as the +2854 pcm the old ring-RPT CSG row showed. That is consistent, and it means THE NJOY MERGE ROUGHLY HALVED THE DISAGREEMENT WITH OPENMC rather than damaging it. The 'baseline drift' would then be an improvement recorded as a regression, and the recorded V&V numbers are stale in the good direction.

PREDICTION, before running u238_recon_fingerprint in both checkouts:
(a) the reconstructed U-238 cross sections WILL differ between 23cd2549 and 0cd9a22c — if they are identical the whole reading above collapses and the shift is in the transport refactor instead;
(b) the 1/E-weighted capture resonance integral 1 eV..20 keV will be HIGHER at 0cd9a22c, since more epithermal capture is what lowers k, and k fell;
(c) grid_points_1eV_20keV will be LOWER at 0cd9a22c, matching the 3.4x speedup — but note (b) and (c) together mean a COARSER grid gave MORE capture, which is not the naive expectation and is worth understanding rather than waving through.

If (a) holds and (b) does not, the speedup and the k shift have different causes and must be separated.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 FINGERPRINT RUN, both checkouts, byte-identical U-238 tape (one sha256 across both trees, so any difference is code).

  quantity                 23cd2549      0cd9a22c     change
  recon_seconds               51.7          23.6      2.2x faster
  grid_points_1eV_20keV     960285        291119      3.3x COARSER
  grid_points_20k_150keV       221           222      unchanged
  capture_RI_1eV_20keV     273.5234      273.6954     +0.063%

(a) CONFIRMED — the cross sections DID change, so the k shift is not purely my DeltaDomain refactor.
(c) CONFIRMED — the resolved-region grid is 3.3x coarser, matching the speedup.
(b) CONFIRMED IN DIRECTION, REFUTED IN MAGNITUDE — the capture RI is higher at the new commit, as predicted, but by 0.063%, which on ln(p) = -C*RI with p = 0.527 implies only about -40 pcm. That is 2% of the -1632 pcm to be explained. My prediction (b) was right about the sign and useless about the size.

MECHANISM FOUND. The njoy merge changed exactly ONE line of outram-mc-libs source (git diff 23cd2549 0dc3e456 -- crates/outram-mc-libs/src): Nuclide::from_endf_file swapped broadr::doppler_broaden for broadr::broaden_result, 'bounded at upstream thnmax (top of the resolved region) so SIGMA1 never runs across the resolved/unresolved seam or over the energy-averaged data above it (njoy op-sdbk)'. That is this session's own thnmax fix reaching the transport path.

Its signature is visible and LOCAL, not global:
  19 keV  capture 1.295651e-1 -> 1.192862e-1   -8%
  20 keV  capture 3.062863e-1 -> 4.054296e-1   +32%   <- the seam
  30 keV and above: unchanged to 5-6 figures (4.344816e-1 -> 4.344800e-1, etc.)
So the change is concentrated right AT the resolved/unresolved seam, which is exactly where a broadening kernel running past thnmax would corrupt things, and it is absent above it. That is a coherent fingerprint of the fix rather than a diffuse numerical drift.

SECOND, QUALITATIVE DEFECT FIXED BY THE SAME CHANGE, and not previously recorded anywhere: the OLD reconstruction returned a CONSTANT inelastic cross section of 2.368721e-4 b at EVERY energy from 0.0253 eV to 19 keV. U-238's first inelastic level is ~45 keV, so inelastic scattering is kinematically impossible there — the old path had a spurious sub-threshold inelastic channel with a suspiciously energy-independent value. New: exactly 0.0 below 45 keV, with the first non-zero at 50 keV. Small in magnitude (2e-5 of sigma_t at 1 eV) but it is a real reaction channel that the transport kernel would have sampled and given an inelastic secondary-energy law to.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and I am not going to assert it: that these changes account for the full -1632 pcm. The RI proxy says ~-40 pcm; a 3.3x grid coarsening and a repaired seam could plausibly do much more through resonance SHAPE (self-shielding depends on the detailed peak structure, not on the integral my proxy measures), but that is a hypothesis, not a measurement. The decisive single-variable test is to revert ONLY the broaden_result line in the current tree and re-run the explicit-cube case: if k returns to ~1.334 it is the data, if it stays ~1.318 it is the refactor. Running that next.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 THE p/epsilon COMPARISON IS INVALID — different conventions, same names. This retires the central premise of this bead.

This bead, and Interpretation item 2 of ring_rpt_vs_openmc.md, rest on: 'the miss is entirely in p and eps... both governed by the U-238 epithermal/fast cross sections', from p +9% (0.5266 vs 0.4842) and eps -6% (1.4131 vs 1.5043). Those two numbers are not the same quantity on each side.

OURS is a THREE-GROUP, leakage-corrected decomposition. src/physics/reactor_physics.rs says so in its own module header ('Three groups, not two'), with group_bounds_ev = (thermal_cutoff, resonance_upper) and p documented as '3-group, leakage-corrected'.

OPENMC'S is TWO-GROUP, split at the 0.625 eV cadmium cutoff. From the committed deck, verification_and_validation/ring_rpt/openmc_inputs/pipeline_triso_to_rpt.py:39-44 and :72-74:
    p       = thermal absorption everywhere / absorption at ALL energies
    epsilon = production at ALL energies / thermal production

THE ARITHMETIC THAT GIVES IT AWAY, computable from the already-published numbers with no new run:
    eta  +0.41%   f  -0.82%   p  +8.76%   eps  -6.06%
    but (p_ours/p_omc) * (eps_ours/eps_omc) = +2.16%
p and eps move in OPPOSITE directions and very nearly cancel in the product, which is what actually enters k. Two large errors that cancel are the fingerprint of a DEFINITIONAL mismatch, not a physics one: shift the epithermal/fast boundary and reactions are re-attributed between p and eps while their product barely moves. eta and f agree to under 1% precisely because they are thermal-region ratios defined the same way on both sides.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is much smaller than advertised: the real disagreement is the ~+1.7% in the eta*f*p*eps product (1.37083 vs 1.34745), consistent with the +1681 pcm (explicit) / +1875 pcm (ring-RPT) absolute offsets. That is the number to explain. The '9% in p' was never available as evidence about U-238 epithermal capture.

FIX LANDED: SixFactors::two_group_openmc_convention() re-expresses the SAME run in the OpenMC deck's two-group definitions. No new tallies — the two-group factors are exact sums of the three-group absorption_by_group / production_by_group arrays already recorded, so it is a re-expression, not a second measurement. Also added OUTRAM_RINGRPT_ONLY=csg to run just the surface-tracked case (~5 min instead of ~40) and print both conventions side by side against the reference. Like-for-like numbers to follow.

SEPARATELY, the oracle for the remaining ~1.7%: NJOY2016 built in-session has produced a U-238 PENDF at 600 K (RECONR + BROADR, err 0.001, matching Nuclide::from_endf_file's tolerance) at /home/user/u238oracle/tape22, 37 MB. Comparing our reconstructed sigma against NJOY's own is the right next measurement — OpenMC's HDF5 is unreachable (403) but NJOY is not, and a port should be checked against the thing it is a port of.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 U-238 RECONSTRUCTION EXONERATED — measured against NJOY2016's own PENDF, not argued.

Method: generated a 600 K PENDF with the in-session NJOY2016 from the SAME tape (reference-data/endf/n-092_U_238.endf, MAT 9237), RECONR err 0.001 + BROADR to 600 K — matching Nuclide::from_endf_file(.., 600.0, 1e-3) exactly. 131,066-point grid, 37 MB. Then compared our reconstruction against it at 19 energies spanning thermal, the big low-lying resonances, the resolved/unresolved seam, the URR band and fast. New example: crates/outram-mc-libs/examples/u238_vs_njoy_pendf.rs (gated, U238_PENDF env var, deck in the module docs so it is reproducible).

RESULT — worst relative difference over the whole probe set:
  MT=1   total     +0.04%   (at 20.87 eV)
  MT=2   elastic   -0.03%   (at 6.674 eV)
  MT=18  fission   +0.14%   (at 1.0 eV, sigma ~3e-6 b, i.e. numerically irrelevant)
  MT=102 capture   -0.17%   (at 19 keV)
Everywhere else, including every resonance peak and the entire URR band, agreement is +-0.04% or better. The 19 keV capture outlier sits just below the resolved/unresolved seam where NJOY's own grid is sparsest, so it is most likely my probe's linear interpolation between NJOY grid points rather than a real difference.

CONCLUSION: the U-238 cross sections are NOT the source of the ~+1700 pcm offset. This crate reproduces NJOY2016 — the code it is a port of — to well under 0.2% on every reaction that matters, at every energy regime that matters. A 0.04% cross-section difference cannot produce 1700 pcm.

THIS BEAD'S TITLE AND PREMISE ARE NOW BOTH RETIRED. 'Cross-check reconstructed U-238 sigma_gamma vs NNDC HDF5 (URR self-shielding suspect)' — the URR hypothesis was already refuted on sign grounds (LSSF=1 means MF=3 carries the infinitely-dilute unresolved values; adding self-shielding REDUCES effective absorption and RAISES k, but we are already high). Now the broader 'reconstructed sigma is wrong' hypothesis is refuted on measurement grounds too.

WHERE THE OFFSET MUST LIVE, given cross sections and pebble geometry are both excluded:
  (a) transport physics — scattering kinematics, secondary energy/angle distributions, the thermal treatment;
  (b) the OTHER nuclides — graphite S(alpha,beta) most of all, since it sets the thermal spectrum on a graphite-moderated system, and f is -0.82% while eta is +0.41%;
  (c) processing-chain difference — RECONR-on-device vs the NNDC chain that produced OpenMC's HDF5 (different probability-table treatment, different temperature handling), which is NOT a defect in either code.
(b) is the cheapest to test next and has the best prior: the same graphite S(alpha,beta) interpolation was found defective earlier today (op-8g54, sigma_inel outside its physical bracket by 4.17% at 3.9 eV before the op-55lj fix).

Note the OpenMC reference was produced BEFORE that graphite fix, and our current numbers after it — so part of the residual may be a genuine difference in the graphite law rather than an error on our side.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 LIKE-FOR-LIKE MEASURED — and it only PARTLY supports my convention hypothesis. Correcting my own comment above.

Same CSG run, both conventions (OUTRAM_RINGRPT_ONLY=csg):
  3-group (this crate) : eta 2.0155  f 0.9140  p 0.5266  eps 1.4131
  2-group (OpenMC defs): eta 2.0155  f 0.9140  p 0.5151  eps 1.4444
  OpenMC reference     : eta 2.0073  f 0.9216  p 0.4842  eps 1.5043

                    p         eps
  3-group vs OMC  +8.76%    -6.06%
  2-group vs OMC  +6.38%    -3.98%
  convention explains 27% of the p gap, 34% of the eps gap.

SO I WAS WRONG about the size of the effect. I wrote that the +8.8%/-6.1% split was 'the fingerprint of a definitional mismatch rather than a physics one'. The definitional part is real and now removed, but it accounts for roughly a quarter to a third. In the MATCHED convention p is still +6.4% and eps still -4.0%. There is a genuine physics discrepancy underneath it and I said there was not.

WHAT DOES HOLD UP — the cancellation, which was the load-bearing part:
  p*eps ratio            +2.15%   (2-group; +2.16% in 3-group, i.e. convention-independent)
  eta*f*p*eps ratio      +1.72%   (1.37059 vs 1.34745)
and +1.72% is consistent with the measured absolute offsets, +1681 pcm explicit / +1875 pcm ring-RPT. So p and eps DO move oppositely and mostly cancel, and the product IS the quantity to explain. That part stands.

NET EFFECT ON THE DIAGNOSIS: the honest statement is now 'our spectrum is harder than OpenMC's in a way that costs ~1.7% in k, and shows up as +6.4% in p against -4.0% in eps once conventions are matched'. Less resonance absorption AND less fast fission than the reference. Combined with the U-238 reconstruction being exonerated against NJOY to +-0.04% (comment above), a harder-spectrum-with-less-resonance-capture signature points at the MODERATOR, not the fuel: graphite S(alpha,beta) sets the slowing-down and the thermal spectrum on this system.

2026-09-11 DIRECTION CORRECTION — I had the spectrum backwards in the comment above.

I wrote 'our spectrum is harder than OpenMC's'. It is SOFTER. Working it through in the 2-group definitions the reference actually uses:
  p   = A_thermal / A_total.   Ours is HIGHER (+6.4%) => a LARGER share of absorption is thermal.
  eps = P_total / P_thermal.   Ours is LOWER  (-4.0%) => LESS non-thermal production.
Both statements say our reactions are MORE concentrated in the thermal group than the reference's. That is over-moderation, not under-moderation.

This matters because it reverses the suspect list. A too-soft spectrum means too much slowing-down power or too little epithermal removal: candidates are graphite S(alpha,beta) transferring too much energy per collision, a graphite scattering cross section that is too high, or missing epithermal absorption. It is NOT 'neutrons staying fast too long', which is what I implied.

Consistent with eta +0.41% and f -0.83%: a softer spectrum puts relatively more absorption in the thermal group everywhere, including in the non-fuel materials, which pushes f down.

NEXT MEASUREMENT, and it is the same move that exonerated U-238: test the graphite thermal law against NJOY2016 directly rather than inferring it from k. Generate THERMR output for tsl-crystalline-graphite (MAT 30) at 600 K with the in-session NJOY and compare our sigma_el / sigma_inel and the secondary distributions against it. THE CONCLUSION THIS FORCES. Cross sections agreeing to ~0.1% while the SPECTRUM differs by several percent (p +6.4%, eps -4.0% in matched convention) means the disagreement is NOT in sigma(E). It is in what happens AFTER a collision — the secondary energy and angle distributions, i.e. the scattering kernel — or in how OpenMC's library discretises them.

That is a real localisation, not a shrug. sigma(E) sets HOW OFTEN a neutron collides; the double-differential kernel sets HOW MUCH ENERGY IT LOSES. A softer spectrum with correct cross sections is precisely the signature of too much energy transfer per collision. Our path integrates S(alpha,beta) directly; OpenMC's c_Graphite comes from NNDC ACE with discretised secondary energies and a fixed number of equiprobable angle bins (THERMR's own nbin, 16 in the deck above). Those are genuinely different representations of the same law and they do not have to agree to 0.1%.

Sample many secondary energies from our inelastic kernel at fixed incident E and compare the mean energy loss and the distribution shape against NJOY's discretised ACE block (acer output, which this crate can write). notes.content:
2026-09-11 THE SCATTERING KERNEL IS EXONERATED TOO — my kernel hypothesis is refuted, and I am recording that rather than moving the goalposts again.

Measured the mean log energy decrement xi = <ln(E/E')> from the graphite S(alpha,beta) kernel, 200k samples per energy at 600 K. This needs NO external oracle: above the bound-scattering regime xi must approach the free-gas carbon value, which is fixed by kinematics alone — alpha = ((A-1)/(A+1))^2 = 0.715976, xi_fg = 1 + alpha*ln(alpha)/(1-alpha) = 0.157769.

   E [eV]   <E'>/E      xi      xi/xi_fg   up-scatter
   0.0253   1.19080   -0.08859   -0.562      15.6%
   0.1000   1.01497    0.01998    0.127      25.7%
   0.5000   0.89721    0.13716    0.869      25.2%
   1.0000   0.87779    0.14583    0.924      22.3%
   2.0000   0.86760    0.16050    1.017      24.1%
   3.0000   0.86390    0.15595    0.988      11.6%
   3.9000   0.86271    0.15801    1.002      11.1%

At 3.9 eV, xi/xi_fg = 1.002 — our kernel reproduces the analytic asymptote to 0.2%. At 0.0253 eV it correctly NET UP-SCATTERS (mean E'/E = 1.19, xi negative), which is right: 600 K is ~0.052 eV, so a 0.0253 eV neutron is below the thermal peak and must gain energy. The trend from up-scatter through the phonon regime to the free-gas limit is monotone and lands on the analytic value.

SO THE KERNEL DOES NOT TRANSFER TOO MUCH ENERGY. The 'over-soft spectrum because the kernel loses too much energy per collision' hypothesis, which I proposed in the comment above, is wrong.

I ALSO HAD A FACT WRONG in the V&V doc and in that comment: I wrote that 'this crate integrates S(alpha,beta) directly while OpenMC uses discretised ACE'. It does not. ICSBEP LEU-COMP-THERM-008 (examples/lct008_keff.rs, commit ec865ef34):
k = 1.02950 +- 0.00061, i.e. +2950 +- 61 pcm from a configuration measured

AND U-238-dominated AND lumped at the same time. Godiva and Jemima have U-238 in

6.674 eV, 434x its 0.39 cm-1 at 5 eV, so the 1.030 cm pellet is 176 mean free
paths across at the 6.67 eV resonance.

The magnitude was PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN, from this bead's own numbers:
I_eff(ours)/I_eff(ref) = ln(0.5253)/ln(0.4842) = 0.888; carried onto a lattice

graphite and FLiBe; and delta tracking -- LCT-008 is SURFACE-tracked while the

physics::slowing_down (commit d5908bf63) solves the infinite-medium slowing-down
equation directly -- the one geometry with an exact answer -- on this crate's own
reconstructed cross sections, and runs this crate's own collision kernel on the
same medium. U-238 + C-12 at 293.6 K, 10 keV source scored to 1 eV, background
cross section sigma_b = N_C sigma_p,C / N_8 over three decades:

  sigma_b [b]   deterministic p_esc      Monte Carlo          diff      z
         30           0.02940        0.02880 +- 0.00037     -2.05 %   -1.61
        100           0.17579        0.17730 +- 0.00085     +0.86 %   +1.77
        300           0.38763        0.38904 +- 0.00109     +0.36 %   +1.29
       1000           0.60543        0.60582 +- 0.00109     +0.06 %   +0.35
      10000           0.88390        0.88402 +- 0.00072     +0.01 %   +0.17

Agreement everywhere, worst 1.8 sigma, and in the SHIELDED regime: read as
effective resonance integrals through p = exp(-I_eff/(xi sigma_b)) the same solve
gives 194.9 / 79.2 / 44.9 / 27.5 / 16.7 b, an 11.7x collapse. A 400k-history run
adds elastic anisotropy and the full production branch (S(a,b) + free-gas target
motion, literally transport_history's own code): both within 0.5 % for
sigma_b >= 100 b.

The solver is checked as an oracle: against the closed form for A = 1 with
constant cross sections (p = c exp(-(1-c)U), reproduced to <1e-5 with SECOND-order
convergence asserted), and against itself under lethargy bisection (0.014 %).

One trap found and now a hard error rather than a wrong answer: U-238's
scatter-in window is 0.0169 lethargy, NARROWER than the gaps a resonance-adaptive
energy grid leaves between resonances. Handed one, the first draft returned
p_esc = 0.00000 where the truth is 0.176 -- plausible in exactly the direction we
were already suspicious of, and it would have "confirmed" an MC defect that does
not exist.

SEARCH SPACE IS NOW ONE THING: what this code does to the flux inside an
optically thick lump. Excluded by measurement: the tracking method (delta vs
surface tracking agree to 18 pcm and the two failing systems use one each) and
the geometry DESCRIPTION (LEU-COMP-THERM-008's core verified pin for pin against

New live lead with the right sign, in op-qho6: the pebble's SPECULARLY reflective r = 3 sphere conserves impact parameter, so b > 1.9 never reaches the fuel; if our specular reflection preserves that invariant more strongly than OpenMC's, we under-absorb in the resonances and report k too high. notes.content: 2026-09-11 ROOT CAUSE LOCALISED (00a095d8d, gh:#188, bead op-77pu). The residual is NOT U-238 resonance escape -- refuted by LCT-008's own independently-critical cases (+2950 / +2271 / +1713 pcm at 1511 / 1335.5 / 794 ppm soluble boron on ONE pin cell; 14 sigma spread, which no p error can produce). B-10's cross section is right (3845.9 b at 0.0253 eV, exactly 1/v), so it is the thermal FLUX where the absorber sits. The water law's cross section is +1 % vs NJOY (graphite +-0.05 %). The KERNEL -- never checked, where graphite's was -- is 2-5.5 % too narrow in <E'>/E and moderates ~4 % too little per collision. notes.content:
2026-09-12 (e97642c5, beads op-i7u9 / op-x77y, gh:#190): the ANGLE hypothesis is
measured and EXCLUDED; a real kernel-WIDTH defect was found in passing and is
worth -63 pcm, so it is not this either.

ANGLE. Every oracle in this crate was an energy-domain FIRST-MOMENT oracle, and
the only assertion on a thermal cosine anywhere was `(-1.0..=1.0).contains(&mu)`.
Two independent oracles now exist: THERMR MF=6/MT=229's 16 equiprobable LAB
cosines per outgoing-energy bin (the records graphite_kernel_vs_njoy_thermr
already parses and discards), and -- for coherent elastic, which has no MF=6 --
the Bragg edge table recovered from the 296 risers of the E*sigma_coh(E)
staircase in MF=3/MT=230, each edge scattering at mu = 1 - 2E_i/E. Worst
+0.0085 absolute on mubar_inelastic, +0.0030 on mubar_elastic, +0.0050 on the
total. mubar ~ 0.05 over the whole range => sigma_tr = sigma_s(1 - mubar) within
0.05 %. EXCLUDED.

WIDTH. <E'>/E is the first moment; the second moment had no oracle. This crate's
kernel is -11 % narrow at 0.05 eV and +39 % BROAD at 2 eV, sign flipping at
0.39 eV. Cause identified: N_EMIT_GRID = 48 over 1e-5..4 eV puts adjacent
emission tables 31.6 % apart and select_table mixes them by ACE statistical
interpolation, adding a variance r(1-r)(m2-m1)^2 the kernel has not got; 48->192
collapses +39.0 % to -2.3 %. PRICED: OUTRAM_RINGRPT_ONLY=csg, same seed,
k = 1.40745 +/- 0.00214 (48) vs 1.40682 +/- 0.00221 (192) => -63 pcm. Real
defect, wrong size. Filed as op-x77y / gh:#190; grid left at 48 because raising
it re-baselines every recorded thermal k-eff.

WHAT THE SEARCH SPACE IS NOW. The residual is present IN FULL in the ring-RPT
pebble (+4048 pcm), which is FOUR CONCENTRIC SPHERES OF HOMOGENEOUS MATERIALS,
surface-tracked -- no grains, no random packing, no delta tracking. So it is not
the double heterogeneity, not the packing, not the tracking, and now not the
thermal angle or the thermal kernel width. The two things in that four-region
problem with no oracle AT THEIR WORKING POINT are:

 (a) the resonance-energy flux inside a fuel lump of REALISTIC optical thickness.
     lump_self_shielding_scan validates the TRANSPARENT limit (-0.51 % vs the
     exact homogeneous answer) and the homogenised control; the thick-lump regime
     has no deterministic reference. The RPT fuel is a 1.4934-1.7531 cm annulus
     carrying the whole heavy-metal inventory -- that concentration is worth
     +3327 pcm over the naive homogenisation on this code's own numbers, and
     nothing checks it.

 (b) any GRAPHITE- or FLiBe-moderated system against a MEASURED critical
     experiment. Both passing thermal benchmarks (HEU-SOL-THERM-009,
     LEU-COMP-THERM-008) are water-moderated. Suggest an ICSBEP graphite-
     moderated case from mit-crpg/benchmarks, by the route lct008_keff.rs
     already uses.

ONE ARITHMETIC NOTE ON LCT-008, for whoever picks this up. The three cases'
offsets track the SOLUBLE BORON, not the lattice: +2950 / +2271 / +1713 pcm at
1511 / 1335.5 / 794 ppm is ~1.7 pcm per ppm, and extrapolating to 0 ppm leaves
only ~+350 pcm. That is consistent with gh:#188 (water kernel too narrow =>
spectrum too hard => 1/v boron under-absorbed) and it means LCT-008 does NOT
evidence a large U-238 resonance-escape error -- a zero-boron LEU lattice is
nearly right. This is arithmetic on numbers already recorded, not a new
measurement, and it CONFIRMS the earlier refutation rather than reviving the
resonance-escape reading. It also means the pebble's +4004 pcm is something
LCT-008 does not exhibit.

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme).

**Fidelity target: All levels**

The flowsheet must provide a **global conservation report**: total mass, C, H,
S, N, O, water, energy, and metals where represented.

- non-reacting unit -> **species** conserved
- reacting unit -> **elements** conserved
- representation change (lumping/delumping) -> mass and elements conserved

```
C in crude + imported carbon
  = C in products + coke + captured CO2 + stack + flare + wastewater/sludge

S in crude
  = S in products + elemental S + stack/tail gas + flare + wastewater/sludge
```

**Make conservation failure loud.** A silent balance error is worse than a
crash, because it produces a plausible answer.

## Validation ladder, and the language to use

- **Crude estimate** -- conceptual flowsheets, conservation testing, rough
  balances, API dogfooding
- **Engineering model** -- measured assay, validated thermo, conservative
  lumping, realistic auxiliaries, validated reactions
- **Predictive model** -- crude-specific assay, operating data, calibrated
  units, validated yields

**Do not label the refinery predictive.** Convergence, material balance and
predictive accuracy are three separate claims.

Every child issue must state its target level.

## Out of scope for this pass (programme-wide)

Do not: port DWSIM UI or graphical flowsheet objects; port CAPE-OPEN unless a
concrete backend requirement exists; reproduce .NET class architecture; make
DWSIM depend on Outram-FOAM; solve thousands of molecular species in the CDU;
implement molecular reconstruction before assay/pseudocomponent CDU works; call
a converged model validated without reference evidence; hide conservation
errors; push to `main`.
